narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which determined an 84% probability that you represent a bad credit risk — a high enough likelihood that your application was unfortunately denied. This decision was driven primarily by the combination of the loan's size, its repayment timeline, and its stated purpose, all of which placed your profile well outside the range typically seen among approved applicants.

To help you understand what would need to change for an approval, the system generated a set of "what if" scenarios — alternative versions of your application where certain details are different and the outcome flips to an approval. Think of these as a roadmap showing which levers, if adjusted, would make the biggest difference.

Across all three scenarios examined, the same three factors changed every single time: the loan duration, the loan amount, and the purpose of the loan. No other factor — not your employment history of seven or more years, not your housing situation, not your installment rate — needed to change in any scenario. This tells us clearly that those three elements are the core drivers of the rejection.

Starting with the loan amount: you requested 6,836 DM, which is dramatically higher than the average of roughly 2,887 DM seen among approved applicants. In every alternative scenario, the amount dropped by approximately 3,879 DM, landing around 2,957 DM. That reduction alone brings your request much closer to what the system considers a manageable credit level.

The repayment duration is equally critical. Your current application spans 60 months — more than three times the average of about 19 months among approved applicants. In all three scenarios, this was reduced by 36 months, bringing it down to 24 months. A shorter repayment window signals lower long-term risk to the system.

Finally, the purpose of the loan matters significantly. Your application listed a business purpose, which represents only about 9% of approved loans. In every alternative scenario, the purpose shifted to a used car purchase, a category the system views more favorably. While you may have genuine business needs, this suggests the system weighs business loans as inherently riskier at this credit level.

It is worth noting that several aspects of your profile are actually in your favor: your long employment tenure of seven or more years is solid, you own your home, and you have no other installment plans or co-debtors complicating the picture. These strengths did not need to change in any scenario, which is encouraging.

The most actionable path forward would be to consider whether you could restructure your request — borrowing a smaller amount closer to 3,000 DM, committing to a repayment period of around two years rather than five, and if possible, reframing or splitting the purpose of the loan. Addressing all three of these factors together appears to be the combination most likely to result in an approval.
